content.text: {"relation": "DIVERGENT", "consensus_summary": "All four blind responses converge on a settled core: in biblical symbolism a 'name' stands for the bearer's essential character, identity, authority, presence, and reputation — supremely so for the name of God/Jesus. Complementary facets listed as alternatives include delegated authority ('in the name of'), Deuteronomistic name-dwelling in the temple, reputation/memorial, covenant ownership (name written on someone), new-name identity, and (as fringe) intrinsic phonetic power.", "book_summary": "The book defines the Name as the covenant identity of a house, constituted by three concrete things appointed by its Head and housed in the ark: the Word (manna), the covenant law (stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron's budded rod). A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood; taking the Name in vain means rejecting, replacing, or removing any of the three. A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house and coming under His authority. The book itself flags the common view (character, authority, reputation) as distinct from its definition.", "consensus_core_identification": "Name = the person's revealed character, identity, authority, and presence; the name effectively stands for the person himself.", "book_core_identification": "Name = the covenant identity of a house, materially constituted by a threefold appointment — word, covenant law, and priesthood (the three items in the ark) — such that misuse of the Name means altering or rejecting one of these three components.", "core_relation": "CONTRADICTS", "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION", "boundary_disagreement": "The book retains some consensus-covered cases (the bride taking the husband's name as covenant belonging, echoing the consensus 'covenant ownership' alternative; the name dwelling in the temple, echoing 'Name theology'), but reclassifies key cases: 'taking the name in vain' (Ex 20:7) is no longer about dishonoring God's person in speech or misusing his reputation, but about rejecting/replacing the word, covenant, or priesthood; and the 'name' for which the house is built is identified with the ark's three contents rather than with God's presence or character as such.", "material_contradiction": "The consensus identifies the name with the person's character/essence — the name virtually is the person. The book replaces this with a structural-institutional definition: the name is a specific threefold covenant apparatus (word, manna; law, tables; priesthood, rod) belonging to a house. The book explicitly sets its definition against the 'commonly taught' character/authority/reputation view. Under the book's reading, a person could honor God's character and reputation yet still 'take the name in vain' by holding a substitute priesthood or covenant — a claim the consensus reading does not make and cannot accommodate without abandoning its identification of name-as-person.", "rationale": "Reduced to cores, the consensus says the name symbolizes the bearer's character/identity/authority; the book says the Name is the covenant identity of a house composed of three enumerated, concrete appointments. Though the book borrows the word 'identity' and overlaps with the 'name dwelling in the house' and 'covenant belonging' alternatives at the edges, its central identification relocates the referent from the person's revealed nature to a threefold institutional constitution, and it re-reads the third-commandment prohibition accordingly. None of the blind responses' primary meanings or alternatives identifies the name with the ark's contents (word/covenant/priesthood). Because the book's own common-view note treats the consensus reading as something it supersedes, and its reinterpretation of vain-taking cannot be true simultaneously with the standard reading in the same sense, this is replacement rather than boundary refinement. It is not NOVEL because it directly engages and displaces the recognized consensus rather than addressing an uncovered question.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "One could argue REFINED: the book preserves the consensus category of 'identity' and 'authority' (the bride comes under the Husband's authority) and merely specifies concretely what constitutes God's covenant identity, building on the recognized Name-theology alternative (the house built 'for my name' containing the ark, 1 Kgs 8:20-21; Heb 9:4). On that view the three items are the concrete content of the character/authority the consensus speaks of, making this a precision-adding narrowing rather than a contradiction. The counter is that the book's re-definition of 'taking the name in vain' and its counterfeit-Name test operate on cases the consensus reading classifies entirely differently, which goes beyond boundary adjustment.", "confidence": "medium"}
